budget.scope: incremental metered OpenRouter spend only (Jev + product companion)

basis: Price: OpenRouter's own model endpoint GET /api/v1/models/typesafe/jev-1.13/endpoints reports pricing.prompt 0.000000042 per input token (= $0.042 per million), pricing.completion 0, and NO per-request price field. Cross-checked against the documented worked example in OpenRouter's Jev tutorial: 476 input tokens billed $0.000019992, which is exactly 476 x 0.000000042.

Token ceiling: the bound is the largest documented maximum input a single request may carry, so it covers the COMPLETE request - model, state, questions, instructions and every criteria description - without depending on a tokenizer we have no specification for. OpenRouter reports context_length 32000 for the served model; TypeSafe's own models page is reported as 64000 per request (32000 for state plus the longest question). The two disagree, so the larger is used.

NOT claimed: that payload bytes bound tokens; that the returned model identifier proves immutable weights; that a request exceeding the limit is rejected rather than truncated - OpenRouter documents neither that behaviour nor any billing overhead or minimum charge. The bound assumes only that billed input tokens cannot exceed the maximum input a request may carry, and that no undocumented per-request surcharge exists. It is admission control, not a prediction of actual cost; actual cost is whatever the provider reports.
